scenes.text: A nuclear plant splits atoms to make heat. But most of that heat never becomes electricity.
For U.S. nuclear plants in 2025, the EIA's numbers work out to about 33 percent efficiency.
The rest is cooled away, in cooling towers, lakes, rivers, or the ocean.
The power lines are thriftier. Transmission and distribution lost about 5 percent from 2018 through 2022, the EIA estimates.
So the big loss happens at the plant. Follow the full trip on The Hidden Grid.
